architecturalQuestionAnsweredFromFrozenM.OWED_FACT_PRESERVATION: REQUIRED and fully specified — the contract refuses a verdict omitting a declaration, refuses an out-of-set binding, and permits no route to COVERED but an admitted binding.
architecturalQuestionAnsweredFromFrozenM.ADDITIVE_GAP_DISCOVERY_RECALL: PERMITTED, NEVER REQUIRED, and never given a target. nominatedFact is nullable with no admission code for its absence; the instruction's inherited 'THE ANSWER IS USUALLY NO' prior is the opposite of a recall target; and the verifier's jurisdiction is explicitly bounded to the clarification set, not hazard re-analysis.
architecturalQuestionAnsweredFromFrozenM.consequence: On preservation, draw 6 is indistinguishable from the other five. On discovery, it differs — but that axis has no contractual requirement, no threshold and no measurement basis, so the difference cannot be scored as a contract violation.
architecturalQuestionAnsweredFromFrozenM.measurementCaution: if discovery becomes a scored axis its denominator is human-confirmed independently valid gaps. Exactly ONE has ever been confirmed, on ONE row. A 5-of-6 figure on that denominator is not a recall rate.

compoundQuestion.governanceGapFound: the §165 budget rule governs how HazLenz ASSEMBLES questions from surviving owed facts. It does NOT govern the single `question` string the verifier returns, and nothing in the v3 contract inspects that string for compound structure — MORE_THAN_ONE_PROPOSED_CLARIFICATION refuses an ARRAY, not two questions inside one string.
compoundQuestion.note: two of the four §165 combination conditions are not met on the face of the record. Whether that is decisive is the adjudication.

thirdArmAnalysis.causalQuestion: would richer owed-fact context alone have eliminated target displacement, without any binding protocol?
thirdArmAnalysis.decisiveReason: the answer cannot change the architecture decision. TARGET_COVERAGE_WARNING is a set difference over DECLARED bindings; without a binding declaration there is no set to difference, and coverage would need a semantic matcher — exactly what §160 retired and what §164's central idea exists to avoid. The binding protocol is retained under BOTH possible outcomes.
thirdArmAnalysis.minimumFalsifyingDesign: 6 draws on HS-A1 only, v2 instruction+contract with the v3 owed-fact block present but no bindingFactKey and no declaration requirement; ~$0.34 worst case
thirdArmAnalysis.whyNotWorthItNow: the binding blocker is silence-side truth, which blocks EVERY precision claim and customer activation, and has been unresolved for three operations. Attribution blocks one phrasing of one claim and no activation.
